continuity_scope: Square Enix's launch-release Tactics Ogre: Reborn for PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch, and Steam, dated 11 November 2022. The character witness is Square Enix's Japanese official product page; its Roman-alphabet display names are retained where they differ from other localizations. The pass is version-specific: it does not silently merge the 1995 Tactics Ogre, the PSP Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together, later patches, or other Ogre Battle works. It relates to SRC-127 only as a versioned reworking within the broader Ogre Battle/Tactics Ogre source family.

coverage_rule: Include every individually named, non-generic character profile in the selected official Japanese product page's displayed Character module: Denim Powell, Catiua Powell, Vyce Bozeck, Lanselot Hamilton, Warren Moon, Canopus Wolph, Mirdyn Walhorn, and Gildas W. Byrne. Include only relationships directly stated in those profiles. Jobs/classes, orders, peoples, named political groups, elements, equipment, spells, tarot, maps, victory conditions, and gameplay systems remain dimensions or source terms and never become character nodes. This rule is complete for that eight-profile web module, not for the full branching game cast.
omissions: Every named character not displayed in the selected official Character module, including Dorgalua, Tristan, Prancet, and antagonists or recruits named only in story, maps, route-exclusive scenes, Warren Report entries, postgame material, or other promotional assets
All player-generated, generic, and collectively described units
Jobs/classes, orders, peoples, factions, elements, weapons, magic, deities, tarot cards, equipment, battle objectives, and the Valerian Isles as non-character graph nodes
The 1995 original, the PSP version, other Ogre Battle titles, and post-launch changes not independently versioned in the cited material
uncertainties: Square Enix's cited release/support materials identify the release date and platforms but do not publish an executable build number; this is consequently bounded as the 11 November 2022 launch release, not a numbered patch snapshot.

The Japanese product page uses Roman-alphabet character names such as Denim Powell and Warren Moon, whereas other localizations use different spellings. This pass retains the selected witness's names and does not normalize them by fan sources.
The game has a branching narrative whose choices can make allies become foes; absent claim-specific scene/codex locators, no route-dependent relationship is inferred beyond the profile statements.

The official page says Reborn restores elements from the original Tactics Ogre and changes the class-level system used in Tactics Ogre: Wheel of Fortune. That establishes versioned adaptation context, not mechanical identity with SRC-127.
evidence_basis: First-party Square Enix materials only. The Japanese product page supplies the bounded character profiles and its System section documents Reborn-specific unit-level progression and inherited/returned systems. The English launch announcement identifies Denam Pavel's Walister-resistance premise, and the English systems article documents the release's multi-scenario, classes, elements, tarot, and RT terminology. The support article fixes the published release date and platforms.
